title: When a Continuation Supply Starts Counting — Prescription Insurance on File Billing Clause
content:
**C1. Principle.** Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, a continuation supply starts when the patient's current cover runs out.

**C2. Approved supply remaining.** The continued drug is the prescription the most recent denial on the coverage concerns. The approved supply remaining on the date of service is the days supply billed on the most recent claim paid for the continued drug under a prior authorization approval, less the calendar days from that claim's date of service to the continuation's date of service, never less than 0.

**C3. Where the count starts.**

(a) While the most recent approval on the coverage still runs past the date of service, the count starts the day after its approval end date, so the calendar days from the date of service to that approval end date are taken off the continuation days supply.

(b) Once that approval has run out but approved supply remains on the date of service, the count starts the day after that supply runs out, so the days of approved supply remaining are taken off.

(c) Otherwise the count starts on the date of service and nothing is taken off.

An approval "still runs past the date of service" when its approval end date is at least one day after the date of service; an approval ending on the date of service has run out.

## Worked cases (hypothetical, date of service 10 June)

| Most recent approval ends | Most recent approved claim | Approved supply remaining | Start of count | Days taken off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14 June | any | — | 15 June | 4 |
| 10 June | 30 days on 20 May | 30 less 21: 9 | 20 June | 9 |
| 5 June | 30 days on 20 May | 9 | 20 June | 9 |
| 5 June | 30 days on 5 May | 30 less 36: below 0, so 0 | 10 June | 0 |
